claim: GraphPlugin Protocol's full provenance, traced to primary sources in orama-system (not PT), recorded here for cross-repo traceability since the investigation started from a PT-adjacent MiniGraph reconciliation effort. Chain, each link verified via git metadata directly, not inferred: docs/v2/05-feasibility-review.md (orama-system, created 2026-05-01 by cyre) first names the exact method signatures on_node_start/on_node_end, recommending a formal GraphPlugin protocol specifically to prevent plugins "monkey-patching the ainvoke loop" and to give the SqliteCheckpointer and HITL Interrupts plugins "documented hooks" instead of reaching into MiniGraph internals directly -- an explicitly named leaky-abstraction concern, not an arbitrary design choice. docs/v2/08-technical-architecture-review.md (orama-system, created 2026-05-02, same commit 4ae30fe6/32d32743/19e948d5 that added GraphPlugin to 01-kernel-spec.md) implements 05's recommendation near-verbatim in its own section F1, and its title literally contains "(Gemini-Analyzer)" -- an explicit label, not informal attribution -- naming the AI collaborator used for this synthesis pass, committed under cyre's own git identity (same pattern as Kimi/Codex/Grok elsewhere in this ecosystem: a human using an AI collaborator, then committing the output themselves). F1's own stated rationale is standardizing an internal SPI for exactly two named consumers (Checkpointer, Interrupts), explicitly framed as differentiating from LangGraph/CrewAI's own patterns ("succeeds where other frameworks fail"), not mimicking either -- an earlier hypothesis that GraphPlugin was modeled on LangChain's BaseCallbackHandler is not supported by the primary source and should not be treated as established.

decisions.notes: Explicit direct instruction to save this for full context and traceability, plus a genuine architectural correction (the fan-out synthesis) surfaced by direct pushback that should not be lost.
